candidates.angle: Krishna sorts worshippers into two destinations

en.intro: Krishna is drawing a clear line here. Listen to how he sorts the results of worship.
en.notice: Krishna says those with limited understanding get limited rewards. Worshippers of the gods reach the gods. His devotees reach him.
en.next: The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.
en.meaning: But the reward gained by those of limited understanding is finite. Those who worship the radiant beings go to the radiant beings; my devotees come to me.

hi.intro: कृष्ण यहाँ एक स्पष्ट रेखा खींचते हैं। सुनिए, वे पूजा के परिणामों को कैसे अलग करते हैं।
hi.meaning: परन्तु उन अल्पबुद्धिवाले मनुष्योंको उन देवताओंकी आराधनाका फल अन्तवाला नाशवान् ही मिलता है । देवोंका पूजन करनेवाले देवोंको प्राप्त होते हैं और मेरे भक्त मेरे ही प्राप्त होते हैं ॥
hi.notice: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि अल्पमेधस, कम बुद्धिवाले, सीमित फल पाते हैं। देवों का पूजन करनेवाले देवोंको जाते हैं। मेरे भक्त मुझे पाते हैं।
hi.next: अज्ञानी लोग सोचते हैं कि मैंने अनदेखे से दृश्य रूप धारण किया है, वे मेरी अविनाशी परम प्रकृति को नहीं जानते।

issues: unsupported: "कृष्ण पूछते हैं कि किस बुद्धि से मनुष्य उनके अनदेखे रूप को देख सकता है।" (The Hindi 'next' states that Krishna asks what kind of mind can see his unseen form. However, verse 24 (the actual next verse) says 'The unwise think I have taken a visible form from the unseen. They do not know my imperishable, supreme nature.' The next verse does not contain a question from Krishna about how one can see his unseen form. This is a factual claim unsupported by the source.)

borrowed: "Worshippers of the gods reach the gods, but his devotees reach him." (The English 'notice' borrows the core contrast of verse 23 and presents it as if it were the content of the 'notice' for this verse, but it is actually a summary of the verse itself. More critically, the Hindi 'notice' contains the phrase 'पर मेरे भक्त मुझे पाते हैं' which directly states the content of verse 23. However, the 'next' field in the English script is a direct copy of verse 24. The Hindi 'notice' is severely problematic because it states 'देवों का पूजन करनेवाले देवोंको जाते हैं, पर मेरे भक्त मुझे पाते हैं', which is the exact meaning of verse 23, not a notice. It completely fails to distinguish between the verse's meaning and the notice, effectively borrowing the verse's content into the notice.)
